title: Quaest poll shows Lula leading and Cury emerging
seoTitle: Quaest poll shows Lula leading and Cury emerging
subtitle: The new poll reveals Augusto Cury's rise and maintains polarization between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro
excerpt: The Quaest poll released on Sept 2 indicates Lula leads with 37% of voting intentions in the first round, Flávio Bolsonaro has 29%, and Augusto Cury.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The Quaest poll released on September 2 shows that Lula leads the first round with 37% of voting intentions, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro with 29%. Augusto Cury, from the Avante party, appears in third place with 10%. The survey, conducted in-person with 2,004 Brazilians aged 16 or older between August 30 and September 1, has a margin of error of two percentage points and a confidence level of 95%. The survey is registered with the Superior Electoral Court under number BR-07065/2026.

Stimulated scenario results

  • Lula (PT): 37%
  • Flávio Bolsonaro (PL): 29%
  • Augusto Cury (Avante): 10%
  • Renan Santos (Missão): 3%
  • Ronaldo Caiado (PSD): 1%
  • Romeu Zema (Novo): 1%
  • Samara Martins (UP): 1%
  • Undecided: 11%
  • Blank/null/won't vote: 7%

Results without Pablo Marçal

  • Lula (PT): 37%
  • Flávio Bolsonaro (PL): 29%
  • Augusto Cury (Avante): 10%
  • Renan Santos (Missão): 3%
  • Ronaldo Caiado (PSD): 1%
  • Romeu Zema (Novo): 1%
  • Samara Martins (UP): 1%
  • Undecided: 11%
  • Blank/null/won't vote: 7%

Second-round simulation

  • Lula: 42%
  • Flávio Bolsonaro: 41%
  • Undecided: 4%
  • Blank/null/won't vote: 13%

Rejection and government approval

  • Lula's rejection: 53%
  • Flávio Bolsonaro's rejection: 55%
  • Lula government approval: 45%
  • Lula government disapproval: 48%

Cury's impact on voting intentions

Augusto Cury's rise to 10% in voting intentions has taken up space from candidates such as Renan Santos, Ronaldo Caiado, and Romeu Zema, who register 3% and 1% respectively. Cury's growth is attributed to his performance among independent voters, where he reaches 24% and places numerically ahead of Lula.

Voter reaction to candidates

  • Flávio Bolsonaro: 55% know him and wouldn't vote for him
  • Lula: 53% know him and wouldn't vote for him
  • Pablo Marçal: 44%
  • Ronaldo Caiado: 40%
  • Romeu Zema: 38%
  • Renan Santos: 28%
  • Augusto Cury: 25%
  • Rui Costa Pimenta: 23%

Conclusion

The Quaest poll maintains polarization between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, while Augusto Cury reaching the 10% voting intention threshold is already altering the race's dynamics, drawing votes away from centrist candidates and creating a new point of attention for the frontrunners. The result will be monitored in the coming days as more polls are released.

With information from G1, Estadão, VEJA.
